steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Conjugal roles: the roles of husbands and wives within a family. Segregated conjugal roles (Bott): clear division between male (breadwinner) and female (homemaker) roles with separate leisure activities. Joint conjugal roles: couples share tasks and leisure. | Key Fact: Young and Willmott's symmetrical family (1973): the family is becoming more symmetrical - couples share domestic work, decision-making and leisure. They identified three stages: pre-industrial (unit of production), early industrial (segregated roles), symmetrical (joint roles). This change is driven by women working, geographical mobility, and new technology. | Key Fact: Feminist challenge: Oakley (1974) argued the symmetrical family is a myth. Her research found: 72% of husbands had 'no regular domestic duties';

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe Young and Willmott's symmetrical family and evaluate whether it accurately represents modern family life. | Explain how feminism has challenged traditional family roles, using evidence. | Evaluate whether conjugal roles have become more equal in modern families.
